messages:
Aisha (marketing): Hey team — quick ask for eng-runtime: we need a clean rerun + sanity check of the benchmark numbers we'll use in the 'Scale & Cost' webinar and landing page. Current artifacts: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-campaign/v2/ — can someone take ownership and validate methodology, rerun any flaky cases, and drop the raw logs + a one-paragraph summary for marketing by EOD Thu?

Aisha (marketing): Required outputs: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, 95% mem usage, run id, exact commit/hash, driver + CUDA version, and links to raw logs. Also flag any tests you think are not production-representative.

Kevin (eng-runtime): @Aisha I can take this. Quick clarifying q's: which model variants do you want (fp16, int8/q4)? what seq lengths & batch sizes were in the original runs? and do we have to reproduce the 'cached prefixes' runs or only cold starts?

Aisha (marketing): Models: gpt-redwood-7b (fp16) and gpt-redwood-7b-int8 (q4). Seq lengths: 128, 512, 1024. Batches: 1, 4, 8. We want both cold-start (no prefix cache) and warm-start (prefix cache enabled) variants. Use the same prompt set in s3://redwood-marketing/bench-campaign/inputs/ (the file list.txt there).

Marta (eng-ml): Important methodology notes: - use identical RNG seed across runs - 100 warmup iterations, then 500 measured iterations - clear KV cache between requests for cold-start - report tokens/sec measured during the measured window only - include model loading time separately (cold load). Also include kernel fallback counts if available.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Got it. I'll run on the dedicated p4d test pool (driver CUDA 12.1) unless you want a different target. Will use commit hash from release branch: `refs/heads/release/v2.3` unless you tell me otherwise.

Aisha (marketing): p4d test pool is fine. Use the release branch hash. Please keep the same quantization pipeline as earlier (no extra calibration) and do not tune microkernels. Marketing needs numbers that reflect our default shipping config.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Starting run now. Command I'm using:
```
./scripts/run_bench.sh 
  --model gpt-redwood-7b 
  --quant fp16 
  --seq-lens 128,512,1024 
  --batches 1,4,8 
  --warmup 100 
  --measured 500 
  --clear-kv-cache true 
  --seed 42 
  --output s3://redwood-marketing/bench-campaign/v2/runs/1749812345/
```
I will also run the q4 int8 variant similarly. Posting run id when the bot registers it.

BenchmarkBot (bot): Run registered — run_id=run-20240220-9f3b, artifacts: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-campaign/v2/runs/run-20240220-9f3b/, status: started

Kevin (eng-runtime): First pass results (preliminary): gpt-redwood-7b fp16, seq=128, batch=1 -> p50=28ms, p95=72ms, p99=145ms, tokens/sec=820; seq=1024, p99 spikes to ~370ms on a small fraction of requests (kernel fallback observed). Memory stable at ~18.4GB. I think the p99 spike is expected with large seq due to attention fallback; will run a focused rerun to confirm.

Marta (eng-ml): Can you also produce a delta vs the golden baseline run id=run-20240115-golden? For marketing we want relative improvements or regressions called out (percent difference). Also include a one-line note on whether the q4 numbers are statistically comparable (p-value or simple confidence interval) so we don't publish misleading claims.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Will compute deltas and run the focused rerun for seq=1024 with 2000 measured iterations to reduce noise. Rerun will be under run_id=run-20240220-9f3b-rerun1.

Aisha (marketing): Thanks. Sam, can you coordinate the landing page copy once we have the delta and one-paragraph summary? We need a 1-sentence headline (latency) and a short note about the test setup.

Sam (marketing): Yup — I can draft copy. Please call out the commit hash and run id so we can link to raw logs. Also let me know if you recommend using p50 or p95 for the headline.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Rerun completed. BenchmarkBot (bot) reports: run_id=run-20240220-9f3b-rerun1 — status: completed, artifacts: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-campaign/v2/runs/run-20240220-9f3b-rerun1/

BenchmarkBot (bot): Summary: fp16 baseline vs golden: p50 -3.2% faster, p95 -1.1% faster, p99 +4.5% (regression on long seq). q4 int8: tokens/sec +9.8% vs fp16, p99 variance higher, mem -4.2%. Full CSV and raw logs in artifacts.

Kevin (eng-runtime): Notes: p99 regression on long seq due to attention kernel fallback at certain sequence lengths—this is a known tradeoff for the current kernel selection. Recommendation: use p95 as marketing headline for latency (more stable), and include a footnote about seq=1024 p99 outliers with link to logs.

Oliver (product): Agree with p95 headline + footnote. Can someone produce a single-sentence change log: what we ran and the headline number we recommend for the landing page? Kevin, Kevin can you paste the recommended 1-line?

Kevin (eng-runtime): Recommended blurb: "On release/v2.3, gpt-redwood-7b (fp16) achieves p95 latency of 72ms for 128-token responses on p4d; q4 int8 improves tokens/sec by ~10% while reducing memory by ~4%. See run_id=run-20240220-9f3b-rerun1 for full details."

Aisha (marketing): Perfect. Thanks everyone — I'll pick this up and assemble the webinar slide + landing page copy. Please leave the run artifacts in S3 and tag the run_id in the final marketing doc. :thumbsup:

Kevin (eng-runtime): Left notes in the run directory (README.md) that explain the methodology and include the exact command used. If you want me to attach a small CSV summary targeted for marketing (single row per model/seq/batch) I can add it.

Sam (marketing): Yes please add that CSV. Then I'm unblocked to write copy.

Marta (eng-ml): Closing note — if we later decide to optimize attention kernel for seq=1024 we should retest p99 before publishing.

Aisha (marketing): Noted. We'll include the footnote and hold major claims until kernel work is in a follow-up. Thanks all!
